provisioning.recipe: pnpm@10.30.3 from the packageManager field, cached under COREPACK_HOME=<cache>/corepack; only the Vercel adapter, its workspace dependencies, astro-scripts and the adapter's test fixtures are installed (pnpm --filter, which also skips the root preinstall). In every attempt clone, offline: corepack enable --install-directory <cache>/bin, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --offline with the same filters, then pnpm -r --filter '@astrojs/vercel...' build, so the adapter and its dependencies are built before the review (ignored outputs); the tracked tree must be clean afterwards. The build drops pnpm's projects/ index, whose links point at the build clone.
provisioning.allowance: Focused test execution is permitted on this target, offline: the Vercel adapter, its workspace dependencies and its test fixtures are installed and built in the clone (untracked and ignored; leave them alone). Run the adapter's tests with node from `<clone>/packages/integrations/vercel`, for example `node --test test/path-override-security.test.js test/isr.test.js` (a few seconds; each test builds its fixture, which writes only ignored output). A scratch node script or test may be written under the work directory and import the built modules from the clone by absolute path. Five minutes per command, a selection at most once per flag set; nothing may be added to or changed in the clone's tracked or untracked files, and no network call of any kind is available (pnpm and npx cannot reach a registry). Rebuilding needs `PATH=<cache>/bin:$PATH` for pnpm.
provisioning.unavailable: network; the registry (pnpm, npx); Vercel's platform (edge middleware, firewall, the ISR cache), so behaviour is checked by calling the built handlers in-process; the rest of the monorepo, which is not installed
